correctness.rationale: From the explicit 4×4 group addition tables, two separate face enumeration procedures agree on exact cardinality vectors (1,16,48,32,0) and (1,16,48,32,8). The cyclic complex has every edge in two triangles, sixteen connected 6-cycle vertex links, and a fully checked coherent integral orientation, giving a connected closed orientable surface of Euler characteristic 0 and therefore a torus. In the other complex, the saved sequence of 32 elementary free-face collapses is checked step-by-step, leaving a connected graph with 16 vertices and 24 edges, hence rank 9. Enumeration of all four reduced Latin squares and explicit isotopies shows these exhaust all 4×4 Latin squares. All operations are exact and their evidence files verify from the package.

originality.rationale: The claim is a complete homotopy classification of cell-vertex partial-transversal complexes at order four, not a count of full or maximal transversals. Three directly relevant primary texts were materially inspected, including the same-group-parameters homology table of Hämäläinen, whose vertices are Latin trades rather than cells. Indexed literature searches and web searches for equivalent rainbow matching and conflict-graph independence formulations produced no covering implication; remaining indexing and terminology risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent classification under an unindexed rainbow-matching or Latin-square conflict-graph name may exist.
Not every online source was available as complete text; the principal same-object combinatorial and same-parameter topological primary texts were inspected.
Published indexed-result summaries may omit stronger unpublished details; no result was accepted merely because a semantic search returned no exact match.

value.rationale: Order four is a natural complete classification problem: every Latin square belongs to exactly one of two isotopy classes. The result determines both integral homotopy types, not merely transversals or ranks. The contrast is qualitative: the cyclic group table has no full transversal but yields an oriented closed genus-one surface with nontrivial degree-two cup product, whereas the Klein table has eight transversals but has the homotopy type of a graph with free fundamental group of rank nine. The exact topological objects are canonical and furnish a reusable structural benchmark for rainbow matching complexes.
